UnitStatement: OpenPipeStress local-first storage and private path posture for DEL-12-01 is defined by this policy.

The local-first storage policy is a privacy and product-boundary artifact, not a filesystem layout, cloud-service design, encryption claim, secret storage design, professional engineering approval, security certification, or compliance attestation.
The policy does not claim analysis results are fit for reliance without competent human review.
OpenPipeStress is local-first by default.

Private project models, rule packs, material and component libraries, owner standards, company design bases, credentials, secrets, diagnostics, reports, generated outputs, and other user-owned engineering data remain user controlled unless the user intentionally exports, shares, contributes, or attaches them with documented rights.
The public repository is not a default durable storage location for private project, rule-pack, material, component, report, diagnostic, owner-standard, credential, secret, or proprietary data.
The MVP project store/index is local SQLite selected by SCA-003.
The MVP project store must be free to use, bundled or otherwise available with the local desktop installation, and usable offline.
Cloud storage, cloud sync, hosted database, daemon, required network, and cloud service behavior are out of MVP unless separately approved by the human project authority.
Telemetry remains disabled by default and must not become a storage or synchronization path.
Storage choices must fail closed.
Absent, unknown, unresolved, ambiguous, or unsupported storage choices remain explicit warning, finding, or unsupported states rather than silent defaults.

The physical project package/container decision is SCA-003: a local SQLite-backed project store/index storing canonical JSON/JCS-compatible payload bytes and private indexed projections behind application-service boundaries.

Operating-system roots, application data directories, rollback semantics, encryption, secret storage, key management, redaction workflow, import/export formats, and cloud exception workflow remain unresolved unless separately approved.
This policy does not create real private paths, write files, define a product configuration schema, or select storage roots.
The policy authorizes the local-only storage profile, not a public SQL interface.
The core.security.local_first_storage helper provides a deterministic metadata-only guard for storage planning records.

The local_first_storage helper public surface includes StorageRecord, StorageDiagnostic, StorageDecision, StorageGuardResult, storage_record(...), classify_storage_record(...), and guard_storage_records(...).
The helper classifies only explicit metadata.

The helper does not read files, write files, choose operating-system roots, store project payloads, store secrets, open SQLite handles, expose direct SQL, transmit data, authorize cloud or network storage, or implement encryption.
The helper makes no security-certification, professional, approval, authentication, sealing, or code-compliance claims.
Public-repository and shared contexts block private project, rule-pack, material, component, report, diagnostic, cache, and secret storage records by default.
Local-private retention of private metadata requires explicit user intent.
Cloud or network storage markers, direct-SQL markers, secret material, payload material, and concrete path-like details are blocked or reduced to symbolic, safe metadata in guard outputs.
Until implementation selects concrete roots, storage planning uses symbolic path classes only.
Symbolic class PUBLIC_REPOSITORY_CONTENT is public-reviewed and may contain source code, schemas, blank templates, governance docs, and invented examples after protected-content review.
Symbolic class PUBLIC_EXAMPLE_CONTENT is public-reviewed and may contain invented examples or public-permissive content with provenance and review disposition.
Symbolic class USER_CHOSEN_PROJECT_PACKAGE is private by default and holds user project model data in the SCA-003 local SQLite-backed project store/index at a user-controlled location.
Symbolic class USER_PRIVATE_LIBRARY_ROOT is private by default and holds user-controlled material, component, section, and owner/library data outside public repository paths.
Symbolic class USER_PRIVATE_RULE_PACK_ROOT is private by default and holds private rule packs, source notices, checksums, and redistribution status outside public repository paths.
Symbolic class USER_REPORT_OUTPUT_ROOT is private by default and holds reports, screenshots, review exports, and generated outputs selected by the user.
Symbolic class USER_DIAGNOSTIC_BUNDLE_ROOT is private by default and holds diagnostics/support bundles only after explicit user review of attachments and contents.
Symbolic class USER_IMPORT_STAGING_ROOT is private or provenance-gated and holds imported files pending validation, provenance capture, redistribution review, and protected-content checks.
Symbolic class USER_EXPORT_STAGING_ROOT is private or review-gated and holds export payloads pending redaction/export controls and explicit user action.
Symbolic class LOCAL_CACHE_ROOT is private by default and holds derived local cache data; cache contents must not become public artifacts by default.
Symbolic class USER_SECRET_REFERENCE is a secret reference only, representing a pointer to future secret handling; actual secret storage is owned by DEL-12-04 and remains TBD.
These symbolic names are planning classes, not filesystem paths, and must not be interpreted as operating-system roots, repository directories, cloud locations, or default user paths.
SQLite files, write-ahead logs, sidecar indexes, cache files, and diagnostics inherit the same private-by-default posture when they contain project-derived data.

Public repository paths must not be used as default durable storage for project geometry, loads, supports, load cases, solve results, SQLite project stores, sidecar indexes, or project package payloads.
Public repository paths must not be used as default durable storage for private rule packs, owner standards, company design bases, rule formulas, thresholds, inputs, or evaluation results.
Public repository paths must not be used as default durable storage for private material, component, section, or vendor-derived library values.

Public repository paths must not be used as default durable storage for generated reports, screenshots, review exports, support bundles, diagnostics, local SQLite stores, sidecar indexes, or local cache payloads.
Public repository paths must not be used as default durable storage for model hashes, manifest hashes, report hashes, rule-pack hashes, or private-library hashes that can fingerprint private work.

Public repository paths must not be used as default durable storage for tokens, passwords, API keys, license keys, certificates, private keys, signing keys, cookies, authorization headers, or other secrets.

Public repository paths must not be used as default durable storage for protected standards text, copied examples, copied formulas, standards tables, proprietary engineering values, commercial benchmark content, or protected/code-derived content.
Contribution workflows may accept public examples or data only after source, provenance, license or redistribution status, contributor certification, and review disposition are recorded.
Local-first storage must preserve the project persistence baseline.
The persistence baseline requires versioned persistence.
The persistence baseline requires schema-governed payloads.
The persistence baseline requires unit-aware data where quantities are present.
The persistence baseline requires provenance-preserving records.
The persistence baseline requires migration-aware status.
The persistence baseline requires deterministic round-trip serialization.
The persistence baseline requires canonical JSON/JCS-compatible hashes where JSON payloads are hashed.
The persistence baseline treats local SQLite storage as a payload/index substrate rather than domain truth.
The persistence baseline requires rebuildable, hash-neutral SQLite FTS5/BM25 retrieval sidecars.
The persistence baseline requires explicit findings for missing storage, privacy, provenance, redistribution, migration, or validation decisions.
Canonical JSON/JCS-compatible payload bytes remain the domain and interchange truth.
SQLite tables are storage/projection details, not public contracts.

Large files are referenced in place by path or URI plus hash, size, classification, and verification metadata by default, and must not be copied into a project package without an explicit export/review workflow.

The private/public path classification and local-first rules apply equally to first-party code, plugins, adapters, import/export paths, reports, telemetry, CLI runners, diagnostics, tests, private-library mechanisms, application services, and support bundle workflows.
Application services must use the same private/public path classification and local-first rules.
No plugin manifest, adapter declaration, CLI option, imported file, report template, rule pack, telemetry setting, diagnostic setting, or environment default can bypass the listed controls.
Path classification cannot be bypassed.
Application-service persistence boundaries cannot be bypassed.
The prohibition on direct SQL, raw SQLite handles, table-name dependencies, or direct project-store mutation by plugins and adapters cannot be bypassed.
Unit checks and dimensional checks cannot be bypassed.
Provenance checks and redistribution status cannot be bypassed.
Protected-content screening cannot be bypassed.
Private-data controls cannot be bypassed.
Diagnostics and result-envelope warning classes cannot be bypassed.
Rule-pack sandboxing cannot be bypassed.
Report/export controls cannot be bypassed.
Human acceptance boundaries cannot be bypassed.
Storage diagnostics must identify unresolved or unsafe storage states without printing private payload contents.

A diagnostic may state that a path class is unresolved, private, public-review-required, export-review-required, missing, stale, moved, hash-mismatched, or blocked, but must not reveal private values or secrets.
Reports and exports remain user-controlled private outputs by default.
DEL-12-02 owns redaction and export controls and should consume this policy's symbolic path-class vocabulary.
Open decision: the physical project package/container is the SCA-003 local SQLite-backed project store/index.
Open decision: operating-system roots and application data directories are TBD; no OS-specific root or real user path is selected.
Open decision: the DB migration and product schema migration framework is TBD; the concerns are separate and versioned, and migration-aware persistence remains the baseline.
Open decision: encryption, secret storage, and key management are TBD; no encryption or secret-storage claim is made here.
Open decision: redaction workflow and export staging behavior are TBD, owned downstream by DEL-12-02.
Open decision: private-library registry and secret/private-library handling are TBD, owned downstream by DEL-12-04.
Open decision: import/export formats and adapter behavior are TBD; no adapter behavior is authorized here.
Open decision: cloud exception workflow is TBD; cloud storage, cloud sync, and cloud service behavior are out of MVP unless separately approved.
Local-first storage policy and future implementation changes should be checked for traceability to DEL-12-01, PKG-12, SOW-029, and OBJ-010.

Verification should check for local-first, user-controlled defaults for private project, rule-pack, material/component library, report, diagnostic, generated output, credential, secret, owner-standard, and proprietary data.
Verification should check for the prohibition on public repository paths as default durable storage for private data.
Verification should check for symbolic path classes instead of real paths, OS-specific roots, cloud locations, or user-specific examples.
Verification should check for explicit warning or finding states for unresolved or unsafe storage choices.
Verification should check for preservation of versioned, schema-governed, provenance-preserving, migration-aware, round-trip testable persistence.
Verification should check for preservation of canonical JSON/JCS-compatible payload truth over SQLite projections or sidecars.
Verification should check for separation of DB migrations from product schema migrations.
Verification should check for no-bypass rules for plugins, adapters, import/export, reports, telemetry, CLI, diagnostics, tests, and application services.

Verification should check for absence of protected standards content, proprietary engineering values, real private project data, real secrets, real filesystem paths, hosted database commitments, cloud storage commitments, network requirements, encryption claims, and professional/code-compliance or security-certification claims.
